category.name: Ecommerce
category.description: Build online storefronts and manage catalogs, checkout, orders and commerce integrations.
category.audience: Online merchants and the developers or agencies building their stores.
category.audienceRationale: Used across industries by businesses selling online; adoption centers on commerce operations and implementation teams.

pricing.note: Basic storefront plan: USD 29/month billed yearly; promotional trial excluded. Payment processing and apps may add costs.
Core: USD 29/month billed annually; up to USD 30K trailing-twelve-month GMV then automatic Growth upgrade. Payment charges may apply.

oss.name: WooCommerce
locked: First-party WooCommerce Subscriptions adds recurring billing, automatic renewal retries and subscriber plan management through a paid annual extension; GPL licensing does not make vendor acquisition free.
oss.classificationReason: GPL WooCommerce core is free and self-hostable. Tier C reflects first-party paid software extensions for recurring commerce workflows, including WooCommerce Subscriptions. The extensions remain GPL; this is a paid acquisition boundary, not a claim of proprietary licensing. Core one-time storefront, catalog and order workflows remain available without that extension.
serviceLimitations: Marketplace downloads, updates and support may require a paid subscription.
Payments, tax, shipping and other remote services may require vendor accounts, connections and usage charges.
First-party hosted WooCommerce is available through Automattic WordPress.com Commerce; Woo Express is discontinued.

health.rsx: Overall score 6.2/10. Activity 6.0, maintenance 9.0, security 3.4, and license 9.0 are the main decision signals.

oss.name: PrestaShop
oss.classificationReason: Tier A applies to the PrestaShop Project core (OSL-3.0) and bundled modules (AFL-3.0), both OSI licenses. Classic is a free downloadable distribution; Hosted adds hosting, installation and support. Marketplace modules and remote services need separate review; Enterprise source access alone does not prove its additions are OSI.
serviceLimitations: Paid hosting, support, payment processing and optional marketplace modules/services can add costs.

health.rsx: Overall score 5.0/10. Activity 4.9, maintenance 10.0, security 0.0, and license 3.0 are the main decision signals.

oss.name: Medusa
locked: Role-based access control (RBAC) requires an Enterprise commercial agreement.
Single sign-on (SSO) requires an Enterprise commercial agreement.
oss.classificationReason: MIT core is self-hostable; root LICENSE explicitly excludes proprietary Enterprise materials listed in ENTERPRISE-LICENSE.md. RBAC and SSO are licensed software gates, not just hosting benefits. Tier B and osi=true refer to MIT core only.
serviceLimitations: Medusa Cloud hosting, infrastructure, email and search allowances have separate paid plans and usage limits.

health.rsx: Overall score 6.7/10. Activity 5.9, maintenance 10.0, security 5.4, and license 3.0 are the main decision signals.

alternatives.migrationNotes: Suitable for a merchant storefront on WordPress. Built-in CSV tools move product catalog data after mapping the WooCommerce schema; this is not a full-store migration. Rebuild design, checkout integrations and platform-specific apps; plan separately for orders, customers, subscriptions and URLs.

Suitable for a merchant storefront on WordPress. Built-in CSV tools move product catalog data after mapping the WooCommerce schema; this is not a full-store migration. Rebuild design, checkout integrations and platform-specific apps; plan separately for orders, customers, subscriptions and URLs.

Another merchant storefront and back office, with responsibility for self-hosting or a separate hosting plan. Rebuild theme and integrations and validate catalog, order and customer migration. No automatic Shopify app, checkout or full-store transfer established.

Developer-built commerce backend and admin with storefront starters rather than a turnkey merchant SaaS. Budget implementation of storefront and integrations; no automatic Shopify app or complete data transfer verified. Enterprise RBAC/SSO need a commercial agreement.

exclusions.name: WordPress standalone CMS record
exclusions.reason: WordPress is the platform prerequisite for WooCommerce; existing wordpress product remains in CMS. Ecommerce functionality is represented by distinct WooCommerce product.

uncertainties: PrestaShop Enterprise additions and individual marketplace module/service licenses not exhaustively audited; Tier A is scoped to Project core and bundled modules, not all commercial offerings.
